newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slack, interest seen staying thin.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slack, interest seen staying thin.

text.p: Singapore shares were virtually unchanged in early trade on Thursday with dealers seeing no sign of major activity before the stock market's half-day close for the Lunar New Year holiday weekend.
"There's nothing to say," said one dealer. "People are here physically but we're not doing anything."
The key Straits Times Industrials Index displayed the signs of disinterest, barely changed at 2,198.87 after 80 minutes of trade, up 3.09 points.
Volume was a moderate 50.2 million shares producing 107 gainers against 77 losers.
Little new was happening as major traders were sidelined.
Creative Technology continued its yo-yo motion, after topping Wednesday's winners it was heading the losers list at 0220 GMT, down Singapore $0.60 at S$19.00.

Most interest was in Malaysian over the counter stocks, with Genting Bhd leading early gainers up S$0.25 at S$9.95, while MBF Holdings and Promet were the most actively traded on 9.6 million and 3.8 million units respectively.
The Stock Exchange of Singapore closes at 0430 GMT today and reopens on Tuesday, February 11 after Monday's Muslim Eid Al-Fitr public holiday.
